prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: مواقيت الصلاة في مدن سعودية (language ar, right-to-left: column 1 is on the RIGHT).
Grid: 6 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "المدينة" · longest unbreakable word 49px · one-line width 91px
  col 2: header "الفجر" · longest unbreakable word 35px · one-line width 35px
  col 3: header "الظهر" · longest unbreakable word 35px · one-line width 35px
  col 4: header "العصر" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 38px
  col 5: header "المغرب" · longest unbreakable word 47px · one-line width 47px
  col 6: header "العشاء" · longest unbreakable word 41px · one-line width 41px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 360px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"A quick-reference prayer-time table for Saudi cities: one city per row, with five daily prayer times to compare across cities and across prayers.","reading":"Right-to-left: the reader finds the city in the rightmost column, then scans leftward across the five prayer-time columns; vertical scanning compares the same prayer across cities, so the five time columns need a consistent rhythm.","groups":["Column 1 is the row identifier and should be visually separate from the data.","Columns 2–6 form one parallel group of prayer times; they share the same value type and should read as a coherent block, with الفجر/الظهر/العصر as the daytime run and المغرب/العشاء as the evening pair."],"keep_intact":["HH:MM time values must never split across lines.","City names should ideally stay on one line; if not, they must wrap only at spaces between words.","Arabic header words should not be broken mid-word if avoidable."],"may_wrap":["Long city names such as المدينة المنورة and مكة المكرمة at word spaces.","Longer prayer headers such as المغرب and العشاء if the column budget is tight; row height can absorb a second header line."]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[112,49,49,49,51,49],"idea":"Keep the city column at full one-line width so city names never wrap, and compress the five prayer columns evenly, accepting wrapped headers and tighter time cells."},{"name":"B","widths":[70,56,56,59,62,56],"idea":"Weight the prayer columns to fit HH:MM values and most headers intact, while letting city names wrap at spaces in a deliberately narrow city column."},{"name":"C","widths":[112,56,56,59,68,62],"idea":"Preserve every cell on one line, including full city names and all headers, and let the reader scroll horizontally instead of splitting any Arabic word or time."}]}
